security_feature_bypassed: Compile-time gating of the AES masking PRNG force-mask override, which should keep force_masks_i inactive when SecAllowForcingMasks is disabled.
finding: The AES masking PRNG is parameterized with SecAllowForcingMasks to disable use of force_masks_i. However, src/aes/rtl/aes_prng_masking.sv:87 assigns bivium_allow_lockup directly from force_masks_i, and line 104 forwards that value to the Bivium primitive allow_lockup_i port. A directed witness with SecAllowForcingMasks=0 observes force_masks_i=1 producing observed_primitive_allow=1, even though the local AES register description states that FORCE_MASKS is only applicable when SecAllowForcingMasks is enabled.

location_or_code_reference.attachment_note: The detection code and reproduction scripts used for this submission are included in the attachment linked with this submission.

detection_method: CSBC identified the candidate using LLM-driven RTL security analysis, and the issue was independently validated by directed single-DUT Verilator simulation.
security_impact: A side-channel test feature can assert a masking PRNG security-control input even when the compile-time policy says the feature is disabled. This weakens the intended boundary around forced constant masks and leaves a sensitive primitive override controlled by an input that should be inactive.
proposed_mitigation: Gate bivium_allow_lockup with SecAllowForcingMasks so the primitive lockup override can only be asserted when the feature is intentionally enabled.
Add a directed regression with SecAllowForcingMasks=0 and force_masks_i=1 that checks allow_lockup_i remains 0.
Add an assertion or lint check that the force-mask control has no effect when the feature gate is disabled.
exploit_or_attack_flow: The attacker or test environment drives the AES force-masks control high.
The aes_prng_masking wrapper forwards the signal to bivium_allow_lockup without applying SecAllowForcingMasks.
The Bivium primitive sees allow_lockup_i=1 despite the disabled feature gate.
